transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, what made me finally make an appointment is that... lately, after some long days on the construction site, or sometimes after a neighborhood meeting, I’ll come home and just eat way more than I ever meant to. 

I'll go through leftover takeout, cereal, chips... really just whatever’s there in the kitchen. And I don't really stop until I’m uncomfortably full. It's been happening enough that I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
During these episodes when you're eating a lot, do you feel like you're unable to stop or control how much you're eating, even though you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly what happens. Once I start on those evenings, it really feels like I’m just on autopilot. I'll be in my head telling myself to stop—especially since I usually have an early start with the crew the next morning—but... I just keep going back to the kitchen for more anyway. It's like I just can't cut myself off.
When you're eating like this during those episodes, do you feel a sense of distress or anxiety beforehand, or does it feel more like you're just stress-eating to cope with your day?

I think it’s mostly just stress-eating to cope with the day, honestly. I don't really notice a specific sense of anxiety or distress right before I start. It’s more like... I walk in the door after managing the crew all day, dealing with the schedules and the noise, and I'm just completely drained. So I wouldn't say I feel anxious beforehand. I just start eating to kind of decompress, and then it just gets out of hand.
After these episodes where you eat a lot, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for it—like exercising excessively, fasting the next day, or anything else to counteract the eating?

Yeah, I do. Um... not every single time, but maybe a few times a month after those nights, I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just start to panic, honestly. I worry so much about undoing all the work I’ve put into looking put-together, so... yeah, I do make myself sick to try and counteract it.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient meets criteria for Binge Eating Disorder with purging behavior. Recurrent episodes of binge eating (loss of control, eating large quantities until uncomfortably full) occurring after stressful work situations, combined with compensatory purging behavior (self-induced vomiting) a few times per month. The purging is secondary to binge episodes rather than the primary feature, and there is no evidence of restrictive eating or body weight below normal range that would indicate Anorexia Nervosa. The stress-reactive nature and functional impairment from work stress distinguish this from other eating disorders.
